en: Title: *Vanaratnastotra* Author: Āditya Source: Hahn 1996
In the language of India:

*Śrīguruvanaratnastotrasaptaka*. In the language of Tibet: *Dpal ldan bla ma nags kyi rin chen gyi bstod pa bdun pa* (The Sevenfold Praise of the Glorious Guru Vanaratna). Homage at the feet of the glorious guru Vanaratna!

In the land of Nepal, the King of Bhikṣus shines forth— he who is firmly established in the constant practice of the Sugata’s doctrine, most venerable among assemblies of the learned, dense with a multitude of virtues,
possessed of renowned and incomparable fame, and endowed with a vast and profound intellect like the outspread cloth of a victory banner.
One whose sole intent is the protection of sentient beings, who has mastered the treasury of the Mahāyāna tenets;
[the King of the land of Bal-po, a Sugata...]
And established them in constant diligence toward the Dharma.
The ultimate treasury of the qualities of the wise.
The King of Bhikṣus, the profound Vairocana of the assembly.
With a fame that is renowned and without any deficiency, |||
With a mind vast and profound, he unfurls the silken streamers of the victory banner’s canopy.
The physical body, too, is the sole refuge for sentient beings.
The Treasury of Tenets Accomplished through the Perfect Realization of the Mahāyāna.
The elder named Yativaravanaratna, who here is a knower of the non-dual reality of phenomena,
is devoted to discipline, observances, and self-restraint.
The supreme lion-king among the elephants of those who propound the ultimate view;
the one known as the Jewel of the Forest, whose intellect is the highest in ascetic discipline.
This Elder realizes the suchness of the non-dual Dharma; he is perfectly restrained by the vows of the Vinaya and is devoted to them.
O King of Beasts, you are the master of the attacking elephant.
I pay homage to the supreme king of great ascetics,
who has trained people in the excellent method of the Dharma and is solely intent on uprooting the suffering of living beings.
I prostrate to the Great Elder, the supreme jewel of the forest; from him, the king of those who are great in their commitment to the vows,
there arises a definitive certainty regarding the supreme way.
The sole supreme deliverer from the sufferings of birth,
you are the great elder, the most excellent jewel of the forest.
To him who causes all beings to awaken,
who bears a bow marked with the lotus of his hand,
and whose body possesses the splendor that adorns the surface of the earth;
The beautiful, great elder among the jewels of the forest awakens all sentient beings without exception who are free from attachment.
Holding a bow of weapons in his lotus-like hands.
A beautiful body that has become the central ornament of the palm of the world.
The great elder Vanaratna is most beautiful.

The impurity of the veil of both renunciation and non-renunciation, which is the very essence of impurity, has been experienced as the departure of that impurity; by you, who possess the arrow of the hundred thousand marks of non-duality between existence and non-existence.
I take refuge in the Great Elder Vanaratna.
[He who] has mounted the elephant of joy, free from worldly pleasure, and is stainless...
One experiences the stainless and the state of being free from stains.
He has mastery over both existence and non-existence as his focal objects.
The great elder Vanaratna has become my refuge.
Delighting in drinking the nectar of the bliss of cessation and the other [joys], with hundreds of conceptual constructions subdued by the method of passion,
he has ripened multitudes of sentient beings in the hundreds.
To the leader of the assembly, the Great Elder Vanaratna:
"I am pleased with this offering of the nectar of the first joy."
With hundreds of limbs that are joyful, certain, and disciplined,
The great elder Vana-ratna, who acts as a physician, has brought hundreds of gathered beings to full maturity.
He whose face has rendered the hosts of Māra and others devoid of splendor,
whose lotus-face has conquered the full moon,
and who is the thunderbolt for the mountain-like lords of opposing disputants— him [I salute].
The Elder Mahāsthavira Vanaratna,
who rendered the mouths of the hosts of Māra and others tasteless.
The lotuses of the sky tremble, filled with enemies.
The faction that agitates the sense bases washes away the king of mountains of the adversaries.
The great elder Ratnākara, who bathes in the forest.
This *Vanaratnastotra-saptaka* is completed.
This *Sevenfold Praise of the Glorious Guru Vanaratna* is finished.
The work of the Ādityas of the Magadha country.
This was composed by the excellent lay practitioner (upāsaka) named Nyima-pa, who came from the land of Magadha.
This was translated by the translator of Rtsed-thang, Gzhon-nu-dpal, by the command of the Dharma King who possesses [divine] vision, together with golden flowers. || ||
